title: Acceptance and Condorcet probability
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean social choice function. Choose each of $n$ voters' rankings of three candidates uniformly from the six possible strict rankings, form the three pairwise vote vectors, and apply $f$ to each; the three resulting pairwise outcomes are accepted when they are not all equal. The tester's acceptance probability equals the probability that the resulting societal outcome has a Condorcet winner.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps sign vectors of length $n$ to signs
The ranking profile is sampled uniformly from the six strict rankings for each voter
